verdicts.reason: Confirmed against both plans. In slice 4, a TransformFreeze stays `{ pending: true; text }` until the queue end and is compared by its text only (§2.3, §3.9 step 4, D4-23). Slice 5's heldFields covers only entries expected at B and not revalued (§2.5). §3.6 takes a typed value's holds from its 'stored held maps', but a pending TransformFreeze has none. So two kinds of reference hold nothing during the transform step: one typed into A's Why in the window, and those of a B-frozen Why the person retypes (now revalued). A copied sentence starts open (TR-4). transformScopeOf removes only keys the session freezes, and held is not a freeze reason, so T's sentence stays in `open`. The step limits therefore allow Claude's rewording, and no held finding arises. At the queue end the TransformFreeze takes its map from the judged state (§3.10 step 4), so it holds Claude's wording. FZ-4 bullet 2 and §14 item 3 fail mechanically, and nothing in slice 5 covers this: a grep finds no pending or typed-write holding, and the 5d tests only cover typed changes to fields that are already held. I rate it major, not blocker, for three reasons: Claude's rewording is still its own Change item, which needs the person's Accept; the target was a field the person left open in the same window; and the later Reject fails closed (slice 3's frozenChangesOf dialog, or a held stage problem). The sub-claim that 'every attempt is refused' for an open field held from B is overstated: the heldField text tells Claude to restore the value, so that part is only a usability mismatch. The fix direction is sound with one caveat. Holds whose value is text (sentence, Why, kind, stance, source) can be set from the typed commit. Statement and declaration holds need facts, which the typed commit does not have (D4-23), so they need S₀'s facts or must be logged as a residual.

Confirmed. Slice 4's revalue replaces only the expectations on the TransformFreeze's own key, and the plan says 'no held value needs revaluing' (§3.11). §3.12 adds: 'Slice 4 revalues no held value (D4-21) … a frozen card whose reference holds a field a transform changes is simply one more dependent'. A grep finds no `revalued` structure anywhere in the slice-4 plan. Slice 5 relies on 'revalued.held' (§2.5, §3.6, and §2.6 as a requirement on slice 4), yet makes such referrers 'a warning only' (§3.7, D5-12). Holders of this kind are the default. Any Why edited on the board is standing-frozen (D3-44). In a transform-started session, every card outside the selection is session-start frozen. heldFields covers both, at B. The typed write of T's sentence then draws a `held` (changed) finding that nothing excuses: S₀ comes before the typed write, so the two-value rule does not apply, and the one-message drop does not apply because T's own TransformFreeze entry has no finding. A no-Claude step fails ('could not be carried out'). In a Claude step the heldField text tells Claude to restore the S₀ value, which T's TransformFreeze then refuses ('never excused by S₀'), so no attempt can pass. The result fails closed but blocks the person's own change on a common path. That contradicts FZ-1, FZ-3 bullet 2e and the plan's own 5d test ('a typed change to a held sentence passes and revalues'). The 5d builder has nothing in slice 4 to map the name to (§0's S4 rule).

The mechanism is confirmed. Today's planGhostAdoption derives the id from the ids in the model (core gate/adoption.ts:125-127), and slice 3 adds only record ids to that set, so a re-write in slices 2–3 gets `foo` again. Slice 5 records the id when it allocates it (5b) and never removes it ('a replayed write allocates again and burns its first id', §3.2). So these paths write `foo-2`: the Redo of an Accept (slice 2: 'Its Redo accepts it again, and its premise write runs again'), and an Accept after back to review or un-reject. What breaks afterwards: the reducer's move does not check ids, so its Redo stores a position for the missing card; a freeze Redo is refused because planFreeze lists the card under `left`; a queued transform naming card:foo is stale at Submit; and the person's typed tokens to the card show 'deleted card'. Every one of these fails closed. D2-73 already lets a Redo differ from the original (or be refused) when the state has changed, and nothing unsafe follows. So this is a real regression against slices 2–3 and against RF-2 (c)'s intent, but minor. Reusing the item's first id is consistent with RF-2: it is the same card, which `takenOut.card` already restores on Undo of a take-out. The fix would need to restate I1 and to read 5b's test 'a premise taken out and a new one with the same sentence get different ids' as being about a different item.

Confirmed, but the window is narrow. takenIds takes the current card ids, every registry, record ids and `extra` (§2.2). It does not take the dangling names that namedIds lists (`premises:` entries and tokens). The registry records namedIds only in applyRecorded, after planning (5b). Any board write records the subject's namedIds before writing, and a session start records B's. So the only gap is a subject's first post-install write, and only when: that write is an add-node; a card was deleted by hand before it; a `premises:` entry written before slice 5 still names that card; and the new card derives the same id. Post-install, every telelean-made name comes with a write or a session start that records it. Tokens in decisions.json picked from the # list name cards recorded at session start or at allocation. Only hand-typed bogus tokens escape, and D5-11 already accepts unvalidated prose. The effect is that a dangling arrow re-attaches to a card with the same sentence, which is today's behaviour and close to D5-18's accepted 'ids of cards deleted before slice 5 are unknown'. Still, §3.2's 'nothing telelean made can name it' is false for those pre-install entries, and 5b's final design regresses against 5a's IDS_FROM_MODEL stopgap, which passes namedIds and would give `x-2`. Adding the current model's namedIds to takenIds is a cheap fix.
